📌 Rule / Concept: The Subjunctive Mood (Motions/Proposals)

The Present Subjunctive is used in "that-clauses" following verbs that express a formal motion, proposal, or requirement (such as move, propose, suggest, mandate). In this mood, the verb must be in its base form. For most verbs, this means removing the "-s" or "-es"; for the verb "to be," the base form is simply "be."

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the verb moved (meaning to formally propose or pray for a specific outcome) triggers the subjunctive mood.

  1. The first verb "find" is in the base form (not "finds"), which is correct for the subjunctive.

  2. The second verb "be" is also in the base form (not "is" or "is being"), which is correct.

Even though "every soul" is a singular subject, the subjunctive mood overrides standard subject-verb agreement.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  • Parallelism in Subjunctive: If a "that-clause" has two verbs joined by "and" (like find and be), both must be in the base form.

  • The "Every" Trap: Words like every, each, and everyone usually scream for a singular verb with an "s," but the Subjunctive Mood is a "no-s zone."

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"If the board approves the merger, the legal team will draft the final contract."
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"If the board approves the merger, the legal team will draft the final contract."
options_en: If the merger is approved by the board, the final contract will be drafted by the legal team.
If the merger be approved by the board, the final contract would be drafted by the legal team.
If the merger is being approved, the final contract will be drafted.
If the merger will be approved, the final contract is drafted.
options_hi: If the merger is approved by the board, the final contract will be drafted by the legal team.
If the merger be approved by the board, the final contract would be drafted by the legal team.
If the merger is being approved, the final contract will be drafted.
If the merger will be approved, the final contract is drafted.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Passive in Conditional Sentences (First Conditional)
In First Conditional sentences, the structure is: If + Present Simple, will + base verb. While converting to passive, both clauses must maintain their original tense. Present Simple becomes: is/am/are + V³. “Will + base verb” becomes: will be + V³. The conditional structure must not be altered.

📌 Application to the Given Question

If the board approves the merger, the legal team will draft the final contract. Here, “approves” is in the simple present and “will draft” is in the simple future. In passive voice, “the merger” becomes the subject of the if-clause: “is approved.” In the main clause, “the final contract” becomes the subject: “will be drafted.” Hence, “If the merger is approved by the board, the final contract will be drafted by the legal team” is correct. Option (B) incorrectly uses subjunctive and changes “will” to “would.” Option (C) shifts to present continuous. Option (D) violates the first conditional rule by using “will” in the if-clause.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Maintain the conditional type while converting to passive. Do not use “will” in the if-clause of a first conditional. Convert Present Simple → is/am/are + V³ and will + V¹ → will be + V³. Preserve both clauses carefully.

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option C

👉 Replace “all together” with “altogether”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Confusing Words – Altogether vs. All together

The words "altogether" and "all together" are frequently confused but serve different grammatical functions:

Altogether (Adverb): This means "completely," "entirely," "in total," or "everything considered." It is used to indicate the sum or the extent of something.

All together (Phrase): This refers to a group of people or things acting or gathered in one place at the same time ("everyone together").

Things to Remember:

The "Total" Test: If you can replace the word with "entirely" or "in total," use Altogether.

The "Separation" Test: If you can remove the "all" and the sentence still refers to a group being "together," use All together.

Corrected Sentence: The court charged them an additional fee of fifteen thousand rupees altogether.

questions.solution_en:

Replace “felt” with “heard”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Appropriate Sensory Verbs -

In English, specific verbs are dedicated to the five senses. Using the wrong verb for a stimulus results in a "sensory mismatch" error.

Hear/Heard: Used for auditory stimuli (sounds, noise, ringing, music).

Feel/Felt: Used for tactile stimuli (vibrations, temperature, pressure, physical touch)

💢 Application to the Given Question - The object in this sentence is a "ringing sound." A sound is an auditory stimulus that is processed by the ears; therefore, you cannot "feel" a sound in a literal sense. The correct verb to pair with "sound" is heard.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I heard a strange clicking noise in the engine. ✅ Example 2: We felt a sudden chill when the window was opened. ✅

Example 3: The pilot felt the aircraft shudder during the turbulence. ✅

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"The government is going to implement a stringent wealth tax on high-net-worth individuals."
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the following sentence.

"The government is going to implement a stringent wealth tax on high-net-worth individuals."
options_en: A stringent wealth tax is being gone to implement by the government.
A stringent wealth tax is going to be implemented by the government on high-net-worth individuals.
A stringent wealth tax will be implemented by the government.
A stringent wealth tax is gone to be implemented.
options_hi: A stringent wealth tax is being gone to implement by the government.
A stringent wealth tax is going to be implemented by the government on high-net-worth individuals.
A stringent wealth tax will be implemented by the government.
A stringent wealth tax is gone to be implemented.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: “Be Going To” Future – Passive Formation
When a sentence uses the “be going to” future structure, the passive form becomes: Object + is/am/are + going to be + V³ (+ by + Subject). The phrase “going to” must be retained, and “be” must be inserted before the past participle. The tense and meaning must remain unchanged.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The government is going to implement a stringent wealth tax on high-net-worth individuals. Here, “is going to implement” is a future intention structure. “A stringent wealth tax” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. Since it is singular, the correct auxiliary is “is.” The correct passive construction is: is going to be implemented. Option (A) is grammatically incorrect (“being gone to implement”). Option (C) shifts the structure to simple future (“will”), altering the original construction. Option (D) is structurally incorrect.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

For “is/am/are going to + V¹,” convert to “is/am/are going to be + V³.” Do not omit “be.” Maintain the original tense structure. Avoid shifting to “will” unless required.

In English, certain verbs have two different forms for the past participle: one used as a verb and one used as an adjective (placed before a noun).

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the word is being used to describe the "ship" (Noun). It is not acting as the action of the sentence; it is a quality of the ship. Therefore, we cannot use the V3 verb form "sunk." We must use the adjectival form sunken.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 ✅: The Titanic has sunk. (Verb – correct)

Example 2 ✅: We are looking for sunken treasure. (Adjective - Correct)

Example 3 ✅: He was a drunken driver. (Adjective - Correct)

Example 4 ✅: He had drunk too much wine. (Verb - Correct)

block of apartments near the city center

options_hi: The Akshay who lives in a
block of apartments near the city center
is waiting outside to meet you.
questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: The "Defining" Proper Noun –

While articles are usually omitted before names, the definite article 'the' is required when a Proper Noun is followed by a Defining (Restrictive) Relative Clause. This clause ("who lives in a block...") identifies a specific "Akshay" out of potentially many, making the name definite and necessitating the article.

Application to the Given Question-

The Subject: "The Akshay".

The Qualifier: "...who lives in a block of apartments near the city center".

The Logic: Because the relative clause is essential to tell us exactly which Akshay we are talking about, the use of 'The' is mandatory. If we removed "The," the sentence would become grammatically incorrect.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips-

The "Which One?" Test: If you can ask "Which Akshay?" and the sentence provides the answer in a "who" clause, you must have "The" at the start.

The presiding judge issued a directive stating that the defendant _________ remain within the jurisdiction of the court and surrender his passport until the conclusion of the trial.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (c).

Rule/Concept: "Shall" for Official Mandates and Legal Commands –

In formal English, particularly in court orders, legal statutes, and official directives, "shall" is used with the third person (he, she, it, they, or nouns) to express a mandatory command or decree. Unlike "will," which simply predicts a future event, "shall" in this context creates a legal obligation that must be followed.

Application to the Given Question - In question, the context is a "directive" issued by a "presiding judge." This is a formal court order. To express that the defendant is legally required to stay within the jurisdiction, "shall" is the most appropriate and precise modal verb.

Correct Usage

  1. The tenant shall pay the rent on the first day of every month. (Contractual obligation)

  2. No person shall be deprived of life or liberty without due process of law. (Constitutional mandate)

  3. The committee shall meet twice a year to review progress. (Official rule)

Incorrect Usage

  1. The law should punish the guilty. (Too weak; "should" implies advice, while law implies "shall"). ❌

  2. He shall to go to the court. (Never use "to" after the modal "shall"). ❌

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

  1. Authority Keywords: Look for words like Judge, Law, Statute, Decree, Mandate, Agreement, or Contract. These are strong triggers for using "shall" with third-person subjects.

  2. Command vs. Future: In modern exams, "shall" is rarely tested as a simple future for "I/We"; it is almost always tested in its formal "command" capacity.

The organization offered the candidate a senior position in the compliance division.

options_hi: The candidate was offered a senior position in the compliance division
A senior position was offered the candidate in the compliance division.
A senior position was offered to the candidate in the compliance division.
Both A and C
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D)

📌 Rule / Concept: Double Object Verbs in Passive Voice

Certain verbs such as give, offer, send, tell, award, lend, promise, etc., take two objects:

Subject + Verb + Indirect Object (person) + Direct Object (thing)

In passive voice, either object can become the subject. Therefore, double object verbs allow two correct passive forms.

Structure 1 (Indirect Object as Subject):
Indirect Object + be + V³ + Direct Object

Structure 2 (Direct Object as Subject):
Direct Object + be + V³ + to + Indirect Object

💢 Application to the Given Question- Here:

Indirect Object = the candidate
Direct Object = a senior position

Passive Form 1: The candidate was offered a senior position in the compliance division.

Passive Form 2: A senior position was offered to the candidate in the compliance division.

Since both structures are grammatically correct, the correct answer is Option (D) Both A and C.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Double object verbs allow two passive structures. When the direct object becomes subject, “to” is usually required before the indirect object. Banking and SSC Mains frequently test whether candidates know that both structures are grammatically correct.

📌 Rule / Concept: Singular Indefinite Pronouns

indefinite pronouns that end in -thing (Everything, Something, Nothing, Anything), -one, or -body are always singular. Even when these pronouns are followed by a relative clause (like "that was salvaged...") or a long prepositional phrase, the main verb of the sentence must agree with the singular subject.

In this sentence, the subject is "Everything." The phrase "that was salvaged from the wreckage of the ship" is a relative clause providing more information about the subject, but it does not change the subject's grammatical number. Since "Everything" is singular, the main verb must also be singular. Therefore, "were" (plural) is incorrect and must be changed to "was" (singular).

REMEMBER THE LIST: Everybody, everything, everyone, somebody, someone, something, nobody, no one, nothing, anybody, anyone, anything; use singular verbs with these pronouns.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: As the principal entered the classroom,
she noticed the students to whisper among
themselves about the upcoming surprise test.
options_hi: As the principal entered the classroom,
she noticed the students to whisper among
themselves about the upcoming surprise test.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “to whisper” with “whisper”

📌 Rule / Concept: Verbs of Perception (Active Voice)

Use bare infinitive after these verbs; Let, Bid, Make, See, Notice, Feel, Hear, Smell, have, Watch, Help etc.

💢 Application to the Given Question

In this lengthy sentence, the core structure is:

"...she noticed (Verb) the students (Object) to whisper (Incorrect Verb Form)..."

  1. Main Verb: "Noticed" (Active Voice).

  2. Object: "The students."

  3. Action being perceived: "Whisper."

Since "noticed" is a verb of perception in the active voice, the infinitive marker "to" must be removed. The correct form is "whisper"

Corrected Sentence "As the principal entered the classroom, she noticed the students whisper among themselves about the upcoming surprise test."

More Examples for Clarity

  • Example 1: I saw him cross the road. (I saw the whole action).

  • Example 2: I saw him crossing the road. (I saw him in the middle of the action).

  • Example 3: We heard the choir sing a beautiful anthem. (Not to sing).
